prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System: advisory WUI decision support; fuses detections, imagery, weather, geospatial overlays into shared fire behavior assessment. Elements: Caldera Incident Command Portal (Emberhall): primary interface; opens triage case above confidence threshold; records reason per triage decision; marks radio route impaired on bridge failure (Orion manual ack); jurisdiction constraints entered before Drone Pilot Operator briefing; shows crew acks beside aviation tasks. North/South Lookout Camera Masts: hardened, lightning-protected, licensed wireless video, cellular fallback. North captures time-stamped smoke bearing (pan/tilt/zoom/confidence); sends Thermal Spot Snippet to Orion. South supplies separate bearing track for triangulation; produces Camera Cleaning Log. Horizon Ridge Drone Dock (Kestrel): produces Battery Swap Ticket for Drone Pilot Operator. Drone Tasking Service: requests, constraints, status, imaging objectives (footprints, altitude bands, revisit intervals); not flight-release authority; may prepare Kestrel verification task; no launch conflicting with Marigold lane. Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine (Lantern): common event record; traceable recommendations; retains timing, source IDs, model versions, acks; score not fire declaration; perimeter intelligence; may down-weight Smoke Classifier; finds heat/smoke edges/flame fronts/spot fires in orthorectified, grid-registered drone frames. Smoke Classifier Module: smoke likelihood, growth trend, obscuration flag; sends plume confidence to Lantern; produces Ridge Shadow Mask. MesoWest Weather Fusion Node (Brindle): sends Wind Shift Bulletin. VHF Radio Gateway Repeater (Badger): recorded, access-controlled; bridges command, air-to-ground, county; shall preserve speaker identity. Crewline Mobile Tablet: Helitack Crew Leader receives only confirmed released context; acks air-to-ground instructions, reports crews in drop/recon areas. Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console (Marigold). East/West Retardant Loading Pumps: East sends Retardant Batch Slip after metered/sealed load. Actors: County Emergency Liaison: sends Drone Corridor Permit. Duty Detection Officer (Orion): reviews triage; verifies alternate contact for impaired route. Air Attack Supervisor (Redtail): deconflicts before drone launch; checks restrictions vs Lantern perimeter; verifies ground clear before flight. Tanker Base Manager: confirms pump readiness. Drone Pilot Operator. States: suspected ignition; Confirmed Ignition needs persistent cue plus independent corroboration; if airspace

New part:
S112: Analytic results are not displayed as final fireline until confidence thresholds, sensor age, and positional error are applied as explicit map attributes.
S113: The MesoWest Weather Fusion Node ingests station observations, forecast grids, and local quality checks to maintain the wind, humidity, temperature, and stability fields used by the spread model.
S114: Brindle publishes a time-indexed weather update that marks significant forecast changes and identifies which map products require recomputation.
S115: Weather fields are interpolated across the incident area with terrain-aware weighting so ridge, drainage, and slope effects are represented at operational map scale.
S116: Geospatial overlays include fuels, slope, aspect, roads, structures, water sources, jurisdiction boundaries, evacuation zones, and known communications coverage.
S117: The fire behavior model combines the accepted perimeter, recent growth vectors, weather fields, and fuel conditions to estimate short-term spread direction and rate.
S118: Model output is expressed as probability bands rather than a single line so supervisors can see both the most likely path and the practical planning margin.
S119: Emberhall renders the current perimeter, projected spread, resource positions, and decision annotations into a common operating picture with role-based symbology.
S120: The Caldera Incident Command Portal produces the Crew Staging Pin from the approved map layer and assigns it an effective time, location accuracy, and incident identifier.
S121: Operational recommendations are generated from rule checks that compare projected fire arrival times with values at risk, road access, crew travel time, and aircraft availability.
S122: Recommendations may include confirming an ignition, increasing camera monitoring, requesting drone coverage, preparing aviation options, repositioning ground crews, or notifying county partners.
S123: The Air Attack Supervisor receives map products that emphasize projected columns, flight hazards, target areas, and timing constraints without obscuring ground resource information.
S124: The County Emergency Liaison receives a simplified view that preserves perimeter confidence, threatened areas, and recommended public safety coordination actions while hiding tactical details not needed for civil coordination.
S125: Every map product records source time, processing time, model version, analyst acceptance, and supersession status so users can distinguish current guidance from archived assessments.
S126: When inputs conflict, the common operating picture shows the conflict explicitly and requires review before the affected recommendation is promoted for command use.
S127: Suppression planning begins after the Caldera Incident Command Portal promotes an accepted fire location into the operational map and marks it available for aviation review.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
